Affiliate Guidelines

Thank you for agreeing to participate in the Affiliate Program (the “Affiliate Program”) of Ion Research, LLC, (the “Company”), whereby you will help to market and sell the Company’s research use only research chemicals to qualified purchasers. We are looking forward to working with you. These Affiliate Guidelines (the “Affiliate Guidelines”) set out the guidelines and policies between the Company (also sometimes referred to herein as “us” or “we”) and you for your participation in the Affiliate Program, particularly related to your posting on social media.

1. Term. These Affiliate Guidelines are effective from the date of your acceptance into the Affiliate Program and shall continue until your participation in the Affiliate Program expires or is terminated by either party for any reason.

2. Social Media Posts. During the Term, you agree to publish social media posts (“Posts” and each, a “Post”) on the specific social media platforms identified in Exhibit A. The Posts will conform to the specifications and instructions outlined in Exhibit A. We, through the Affiliate Program software (the “Affiliate Tool”), will provide you with the necessary materials, such as the unique tracking link you will need to promote (the “Affiliate Link”), so you can create Posts that achieve the goals of the Affiliate Program. All Posts must meet the following requirements:

(a) Your Posts must comply with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Guides Concerning Endorsements and Testimonials (“Endorsement Guides”), for which we provide you a link in Exhibit B. You agree to participate in any training we require on our Social Media Endorsement Policy, if applicable, which is designed to ensure compliance with the Endorsement Guides. You must clearly and conspicuously disclose your “material connection” with us, making it clear that you are a paid influencer or affiliate. You must place the disclosure in plain sight in close proximity to any audio or visual communications that you make about us, our brand, and our products, and it must be unavoidable. You may not bury the disclosure in a link or place the disclosure in a string of hashtags or other disclosures. We require this disclosure regardless of any space limitations of the platform, where you can use hashtags for the disclosure (like #ad or #sponsored). All specific language and placement requirements for Posts, if any, are set out in Exhibit A. If a platform does not allow for a clear and conspicuous disclosure, you should not use that platform.

(b) Although we want your Posts to be authentic, your Posts should only include factual statements about the Company and our products. We may provide you with a list of verified factual statements that you may use in your Posts. Your Posts should also rely on the materials provided by the Affiliate Tool to accurately use our trademarks and describe our products.

(c) You shall never: (i) make medical or health claims in your Posts (avoid suggestions that the Company’s products build muscle; increase fat loss; improve sleep, libido, or skin; treat or prevent diseases; etc.); (ii) state or imply in your Posts that the Company’s products are intended for anything other than laboratory research purposes; (iii) state or imply in your Posts that the Company’s products are for human or animal consumption; (iv) state or imply in your Posts that the Company’s products should be used as a food, drug, cosmetic, or other household use; (v) state or imply in your Posts that anything contained on the Company’s website should be construed as medical advice; (vi) provide dosage or administration information in your Posts; or (vii) use any bodybuilding or biohacking language in your Posts (i.e., “anti-aging,” “performance enhancing,” “muscle gain,” “fat burner,” “nootropic,” etc.).

(d) Your Posts will reflect your own honest opinions, beliefs, and experiences.

(e) Your Posts will be original and created solely by you.

(f) Your Posts will not include the intellectual property of other parties (besides that of the Company), including, without limitation, any third-party music, photographs, artwork, trademarks, logos, or slogans.

(g) Your Posts will not include any person, or personally identifiable information about any person, other than yourself, unless you receive our prior written approval and have the person sign a release provided by us.

(h) Your Posts will comply with the rules of the applicable social media platforms you use.

(i) Your Posts will comply with the standards of conduct set out in Exhibit B and any other policies we provide you with.

(j) Your Posts will comply with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations.

3. Monitoring Posts. You understand that we will be monitoring your Posts for and to ensure compliance with these Affiliate Guidelines. We have the right to address non-compliant Posts by taking any of the following actions alone or in combination with one another:

(a) Requiring you to fix the Post.

(b) Requiring you to take down or remove the Post.

(c) Terminating your right to participate in the Affiliate Program.

4. Ownership; Grant of Rights.

(a) We are and will be the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to the Posts, including all copyrights and other intellectual property rights therein. We will own each Post as a work made for hire as defined in Section 101 of the Copyright Act of 1976. To the extent any Post does not qualify as, or otherwise fails to be, work made for hire, you hereby (i) assign, transfer, and otherwise convey to us, irrevocably and in perpetuity, throughout the universe, all right, title, and interest in and to the Posts, including all copyrights and other intellectual property rights in them; and (ii) irrevocably waive any and all claims you may now or hereafter have in any jurisdiction to so-called “moral rights” with respect to the Posts.

(b) We hereby grant you a limited license to use the Posts solely for the Affiliate Program.

5. Use of Your Name, Likeness, and Information. You hereby grant to the Company, our affiliates, and each of our respective direct and indirect successors, licensees, and assigns, the right to use your name, image, likeness, and biographical, professional, and other identifying information (including information you provide to us and any other information about you that is publicly available) (collectively, your “Likeness”) in connection with the Affiliate Program, the Posts, and any derivative works we make from the Posts, including to advertise and promote the same or any service or product that features or includes the Posts or a derivative work of a Post, in whole or in Part. You waive the right to inspect or approve any use of your Likeness as contemplated in these Affiliate Guidelines.

6. Payment. We will pay you the commission amount (the “Commission”) outlined in the Affiliate Program Agreement entered into between the parties (the “Affiliate Program Agreement”).

7. Confidentiality. You understand that you may be exposed to information about the Company’s products, advertising campaigns, marketing strategies, and other information and ideas that may not have been disclosed to the public (collectively, the “Confidential Information”). You agree to maintain the confidentiality of all Confidential Information disclosed to you (or which otherwise becomes available to you) in connection with the Affiliate Program and will hold all Confidential Information in strict confidence. You further agree to refrain from disclosing or using Confidential Information for any purpose other than participating in the Affiliate Program. The obligation to maintain the confidentiality of Confidential Information shall survive termination and continue indefinitely.

8. Representations and Warranties. You represent and warrant that you are not a member of SAG-AFTRA. You further represent and warrant that the Posts:

(a) are your sole and original creation;

(b) are not libelous or otherwise defamatory;

(c) do not infringe or otherwise violate any right of any third party, including, without limitation, any copyright, trademark, patent, trade secret, or other intellectual property right, or any right of publicity or privacy;

(d) do not violate any laws; and

(e) do not violate these Affiliate Guidelines or the Affiliate Program Agreement.

9. Compliance with Policies; Terms and Conditions. You shall comply with our privacy policy and any and all terms and conditions posted on the Affiliate Tool’s website.

10. Indemnification. You agree to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the Company, and our affiliates, managers, members, directors, officers, employees, agents, successors, and assigns, from and against any claims, judgments, damages, liabilities, settlements, losses, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees and disbursements, arising from or relating to any breach by you of your representations, warranties, or other obligations hereunder, or otherwise relating to these Affiliate Guidelines.

11. Termination. Either party may terminate your participation in the Affiliate Program at any time and for any reason, with or without cause, by giving the other party written or electronic notice of termination, in accordance with the Affiliate Program Agreement. We may terminate immediately upon your violation of these Affiliate Guidelines.

12. Relationship of the Parties. You understand that you are an independent contractor, and these Affiliate Guidelines, in addition to the Affiliate Program Agreement, do not create any association, partnership, joint venture, employee, or agency relationship between you and us for any purpose. You have no authority (and will not hold yourself out as having authority) to bind the Company and will not make any agreements or representations on our behalf without our prior written consent.

13. Miscellaneous.

(a) Your participation in the Affiliate Program is personal to you. You will not assign or otherwise transfer any of your rights, or delegate, subcontract, or otherwise transfer any of your obligations or performance, under the Affiliate Program Agreement or these Affiliate Guidelines. Any attempt to assign, delegate, or transfer in violation of this paragraph is null and void. The Company may freely assign or otherwise transfer all or any of its rights, or delegate or otherwise transfer all or any of its obligations or performance, under the Affiliate Program Agreement or these Guidelines. These Affiliate Guidelines are binding upon and inure to the benefit of the parties and their respective permitted successors and assigns.

(b) These Affiliate Guidelines are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Georgia without giving effect to any conflict of laws provisions that would result in the application of the laws of a different jurisdiction. Each party agrees to institute any legal suit, action, or proceeding arising out of these Affiliate Guidelines or the Posts in the federal or state courts in each case located in Georgia.

(c) If any provision of these Affiliate Guidelines is illegal or unenforceable under applicable law, the remainder of the provision will be amended to achieve as closely as possible the effect of the original terms and all other provisions of these Affiliate Guidelines will continue in full force and effect. These Affiliate Guidelines are incorporated by reference into the Affiliate Program Agreement, and, together with the Affiliate Program Agreement, contain the entire agreement between you and us and supersede any oral or written statements made by or to you in connection with the Affiliate Program and the Posts.

(d) You acknowledge that you have received and read a copy of these Affiliate Guidelines and understand and agree to comply with its terms. You understand that the Company expressly reserves the right to change, modify, or delete the provisions of these Affiliate Guidelines at any time, and your continued participation in the Affiliate Program constitutes your agreement to be bound by any changed, modified, or deleted provisions.

COMMUNITY STANDARDS
Community Guidelines

Ion Peptide is committed to maintaining a professional, legally compliant, and research-focused environment across our website, social platforms, product review platforms, third-party forums, and any other channels referencing Ion Peptide products or brand.

Read Guidelines
Report a Concern
Guideline Snapshot

Participation in Ion Peptide-related content requires research-only, compliant, professional conduct. Violations may result in moderation, account action, reporting, or legal action.

EFFECTIVE DATE
October 2025
PRIMARY STANDARD
Professional, legal, and research-focused engagement
APPLIES TO
Website, reviews, social media, forums, and public references
RUO
Research-Only Discussion

All discussion must remain focused on lawful laboratory research contexts only.

NO
No Medical or Dosage Advice

Medical advice, dosing, titration, reconstitution, or usage guidance is not permitted.

AUTH
No Unauthorized Affiliations

Ion Peptide does not sponsor, compensate, or affiliate with unauthorized creators.

PRO
Professional Conduct

Respectful, lawful, accurate, and non-misleading communication is required.

CONTENT STANDARDS
What belongs in the community

These guidelines are designed to keep Ion Peptide-related discussion professional, lawful, research-focused, and free from unsafe or misleading claims.

Allowed

Discussion should stay limited to responsible, research-oriented, and compliant topics.

Professional research-focused discussion
General product documentation or COA questions
Lawful, accurate, and non-misleading statements
Questions about policies, ordering, support, or compliance
Reporting content that violates Ion Peptide standards
Prohibited

Any content implying human or animal use, medical benefit, dosing, or unauthorized promotion is not allowed.

Human or animal use claims, including injection or self-experimentation
Medical advice, dosing, titration, or reconstitution instructions
Claims about treatment, diagnosis, efficacy, or medical benefit
Harassment, abuse, spam, illegal activity, or solicitation
Unauthorized influencer, affiliate, or sponsorship claims
MODERATION FLOW
How violations may be handled

Ion Peptide reserves the right to review, remove, restrict, report, or take action when content violates these Guidelines or applicable law.

01
Content Review

Posts, comments, reviews, or third-party references may be reviewed for compliance.

02
Removal or Restriction

Violating content may be removed, hidden, or restricted without prior notice.

03
Account Action

User accounts may be restricted, suspended, or terminated where appropriate.

04
Reporting or Legal Action

Content may be reported to platforms, law enforcement, or regulatory authorities.

01
Research-Only Environment

All Ion Peptide products are strictly for laboratory research purposes. Any discussion, suggestion, or content implying human or animal use, including injection, dosing, self-experimentation, or medical benefit, is strictly prohibited.

Examples of prohibited content:
“I injected this and saw results in a week.”
“How much should I use per kg of body weight?”
“This helped me with [medical condition].”

Posting prohibited content is a violation of these Guidelines and may result in removal, restriction, or reporting to regulatory authorities.

02
No Medical or Dosage Advice

Users may not request or provide:

Medical advice
Dosing or titration protocols
Reconstitution instructions
Stacking, combination, or experimental usage guidance

Ion Peptide does not provide, endorse, or condone any guidance for human or animal use. Any implication otherwise is unauthorized and false.

Recommended response: “These products are for research use only. No usage guidance is permitted.”
03
No Affiliation with Content Creators or Influencers

Ion Peptide does not sponsor, compensate, or affiliate with influencers, bloggers, or third-party content creators. Any suggestion otherwise is false and unauthorized.

Users are encouraged to report content implying Ion Peptide supports or enables human or animal use.

04
Respectful and Professional Conduct

The following behavior is strictly prohibited:

Harassment or Abuse: Personal attacks, discriminatory language, threats, or intimidation
Misrepresentation: False claims about product use, safety, efficacy, or legal status
Illegal Activity: Encouraging or facilitating unlawful behavior, unlicensed chemical use, or patent infringement
Spam or Solicitation: Unauthorized advertising, self-promotion, or affiliate links
Intellectual Property Violations: Posting copyrighted or patented material without authorization
Defamatory or Obscene Material: Content that is libelous, obscene, abusive, threatening, invasive of privacy, or otherwise unlawful

Violations may result in removal, account suspension, or referral to authorities.

05
Our Right to Moderate

Ion Peptide reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to:

Remove, hide, or restrict content violating these Guidelines
Restrict or terminate user accounts
Report users or content to platform hosts, law enforcement, or regulatory authorities

Ion Peptide may maintain records of violations for legal, investigatory, or regulatory purposes.

06
Reporting Violations

Users may report violations by submitting:

A link or screenshot of the content
A brief description of the violation
A message through Ion Peptide’s official Contact Page or email
For faster review, include the platform, username or page, date if available, and a short explanation of why the content violates these Guidelines.
07
User Acknowledgment

By participating in Ion Peptide platforms, you acknowledge:

All products are for laboratory research only, and any content suggesting otherwise is misleading
Posting prohibited content may result in legal consequences, including civil, regulatory, or criminal liability
Ion Peptide is not responsible for user-generated content or interactions on its platforms
08
Legal Purpose

All Ion Peptide products are non-clinical, non-therapeutic, and research-only. Statements implying human or animal consumption or medical use are unauthorized and legally actionable.

09
Indemnity

Users agree to indemnify and hold harmless Ion Peptide, its affiliates, officers, directors, employees, and agents from any claims, damages, liabilities, or expenses arising from:

Posting prohibited or illegal content
Misrepresentation of product use
Violation of these Guidelines or applicable law
10
Governing Law and Jurisdiction

These Guidelines are governed by the laws of New Mexico. Any dispute arising from content or use of Ion Peptide platforms will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of New Mexico.

11
Severability

If any provision of these Guidelines is deemed unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect.

12
Amendments

Ion Peptide reserves the right to update or revise these Guidelines at any time. Continued use of our platforms constitutes acceptance of the most current version.

Compliance & Legal Overview

IonLabPeptides.com | Great Research LLC maintains a research-only business model built around legal structure, product classification, operational standards, regulatory alignment, documentation access, and misuse-prevention safeguards.

Read Overview
View COAs
Compliance Snapshot

This page is intended for customers, regulatory authorities, financial service providers, and legal professionals seeking transparency regarding Ion Peptide’s research-only business model.

EFFECTIVE DATE
October 2025
COMPANY
IonLabPeptides.com | Great Research LLC
PRIMARY CLASSIFICATION
Laboratory research and analytical purposes only
LEGAL

RUO
Research Use Only

COA
Testing & Documentation

Product identity and purity are supported through HPLC and Mass Spectrometry testing.

SAFE
Misuse Monitoring

OPERATIONAL STANDARDS
Built for research-only transparency

This overview should feel more like a formal compliance dossier than a simple policy page. The goal is to clearly show how Ion Peptide defines product use, labels products, supports documentation, communicates boundaries, and monitors for misuse.

Research-focused classification

Ion Peptide products are not presented for clinical, therapeutic, diagnostic, compounding, dietary supplement, cosmetic, human, or veterinary use.

Documentation-backed operations

Certificates of Analysis are available for download on product listings, and shipments include printed or digital access to relevant COA documentation.

Clear misuse boundaries

Ion Peptide does not provide dosing, preparation, reconstitution, injection, administration, storage-for-consumption, or usage guidance.

COMPLIANCE FLOW
How the compliance system is framed

These checkpoints help communicate the site’s research-use-only position in a clean, easy-to-scan way without making the legal page feel crowded.

01
Define Classification

Products are positioned strictly for laboratory research and analytical purposes.

02
Label Clearly

RUO labeling and disclaimers are applied across labels, checkout, and packaging.

03
Document Quality

Testing documentation supports product identity, purity, and shipment records.

04
Monitor Misuse

Suspicious or non-research activity may trigger order or account-level action.

01
Company Legal Structure

IonLabPeptides.com | Great Research, LLC is a New Mexico-based Limited Liability Company, registered and in good standing. Our business operates exclusively as a research chemical supplier.

We are not a pharmacy, compounding facility, or health product distributor, and we do not market products for human or veterinary use.

02
Intended Use of Products

All products sold by IonLabPeptides.com are strictly for laboratory research and analytical purposes.

They are:

Not approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
Not intended for human or animal consumption or use
Not for therapeutic, diagnostic, or medical purposes
Not to be compounded, repackaged, or resold as drugs, dietary supplements, or cosmetics

These restrictions are clearly disclosed on:

Our Terms of Service
Product labels
Checkout disclaimers
Packaging inserts
03
FDA Compliance — Research Use Only (RUO)

All products are labeled in accordance with 21 CFR 809.10(c)(2)(i) as Research Use Only (RUO). They are not intended for clinical investigations or diagnostic applications.

RUO-specific labeling includes:

“For Research Use Only”
“Not for Human or Animal Use”
No dosing, reconstitution, or administration instructions provided
Ion Peptide’s RUO position is intended to prevent product misclassification, misuse, or interpretation as clinical, therapeutic, diagnostic, or consumer-use products.
04
Product Testing & Documentation

Every product undergoes rigorous testing via HPLC and Mass Spectrometry to confirm identity and purity.

Certificates of Analysis (COAs) are available for download on product listings
Every shipment includes either a printed COA or a digital link to the relevant COA
05
Packaging, Labeling, and Shipment
Products are shipped in tamper-evident, RUO-labeled packaging
Packaging excludes medically symbolic or injection-related language
COAs and RUO disclaimers are included with all shipments
Shipments use generic, discreet exterior boxes
Any included bacteriostatic water is labeled: “For Laboratory Research Use Only. Not for injection or clinical use.”
06
Communication & Customer Support Policy

IonLabPeptides.com does not provide guidance on:

Dosing
Preparation or reconstitution
Injection or administration
Storage for consumption

Any inquiries regarding these topics are redirected to our Terms of Service and Community Guidelines.

07
Enforcement, Monitoring & Misuse Reporting

We actively monitor for product misuse and take appropriate measures.

Canceling suspicious or non-research orders
Restricting or banning customers who violate Terms
Disclaiming responsibility for third-party content
Cooperating with authorities if unlawful use is identified
All customers agree to indemnify IonLabPeptides.com from misuse-related liability at checkout.
08
Regulatory & Financial Platform Cooperation

This page is designed to support:

Payment processors including Shopify, Square, and Stripe
Shipping partners
Regulatory authorities
Industry watchdogs

We maintain this page publicly to promote transparency and reduce the risk of product misclassification.

09
Contact & Documentation Requests

For additional documentation, verification of COAs, or copies of our legal policies, please contact:

Email: support@ionlabpeptides.com

Our Mission
MEDICAL RESEARCH DONATION INITIATIVE
Supporting the Future of Medical Research

At Ion Peptide, research advancement is at the core of what we do. We believe innovation, discovery, and progress are driven by the researchers, scientists, doctors, and organizations working every day to improve lives.

OUR MISSION
Putting action behind research values.

This initiative is our way of putting action behind our values. We are proud to support organizations focused on important areas such as childhood cancer, blood cancer, Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, cancer research, and broader medical research.

Every breakthrough starts with support — support for ideas, support for studies, support for researchers, and support for the organizations helping push medicine forward.

Our goal is simple: to help fund meaningful research that can make a real difference.

WHY WE’RE DOING THIS
Research moves the world forward.

We work closely with the research community, and we understand how important funding is to continued progress. Medical research depends on consistent support, serious organizations, and people willing to invest in future breakthroughs.

This is not a one-time gesture. It is a long-term commitment to helping support the people and organizations working toward better treatments, better outcomes, and a healthier future.

Monthly donations help qualified organizations continue research-focused work.

Each month, Ion Peptide will review qualified medical research-based organizations and give the community an opportunity to help decide where the donation should go.

✓

✓

Research confidence and precision

From biomedical studies to pharmaceutical development, IonPeptide peptides support scientific progress worldwide. BY PEPTIDE INFORMATION

At IonLabPeptides.com, we believe that knowledge is power — especially when it comes to science. Our peptides are offered exclusively for in-vitro research purposes, giving scientists reliable tools to explore breakthroughs in medicine, biology, and biotechnology.

Important Notice: Our peptides are not approved for human or animal use, nor are they intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. They are strictly for laboratory research and educational applications.

What is a Peptide?

A peptide is a naturally occurring chain of amino acids — the fundamental building blocks of proteins — linked together by strong chemical bonds. Think of them as tiny molecular messengers that play a crucial role in countless biological processes.

Peptides are formed when two or more amino acids connect through a bond called a peptide bond. This happens in a natural process where water is released, resulting in a stable chain that can influence everything from cell communication to hormone regulation.

The word “peptide” comes from the Greek word meaning “to digest,” which reflects how central they are to life and health. Thousands of peptides are already at work in the human body, supporting growth, healing, and normal function.

Thanks to modern science, researchers can now create peptides in the lab to study their effects and develop new applications. These discoveries hold exciting promise for the future of medicine, nutrition, and pharmaceutical innovation.

How Are Peptides Formed?

Peptides are created both naturally in the body and synthetically in the lab.

Inside the body, peptides are produced through normal biological processes — including the creation of ribosomal and non-ribosomal peptides that regulate essential functions like hormones and signaling pathways.

In the lab, scientists use advanced peptide synthesis techniques to design and create custom peptides for research. Two common approaches are:

Liquid-Phase Peptide Synthesis
Used for certain specialized applications.
Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis
The gold standard in research and commercial production due to its precision and efficiency.

Thanks to these innovations, researchers can now create virtually unlimited peptide sequences to explore new discoveries in medicine, nutrition, and biotechnology.

Peptide formation joins amino acids through peptide bonds, creating a stable amino acid chain.
Fun Fact: The very first synthetic peptide was created in 1901 by Emil Fischer and Ernest Fourneau. Later, in 1953, Vincent du Vigneaud synthesized oxytocin — the first-ever polypeptide hormone.
Peptide Terminology

Peptides are grouped based on the number of amino acids they contain:

Dipeptide
Just 2 amino acids.
Tripeptide
3 amino acids.
Oligopeptide
Short chains, usually fewer than 10 amino acids.
Polypeptide
Longer chains, 10+ amino acids.
Proteins
Very long chains — typically more than 40–50 amino acids.

In short, peptides are simply shorter chains of amino acids, while proteins are the longer, more complex versions.

There are exceptions, though — some very long peptides are still considered peptides, while some small proteins, like insulin, are commonly referred to as peptides.

Classification of Peptides

Peptides can be grouped into several main categories based on how they are created and where they are found.

Ribosomal Peptides
These are made naturally by the body when cells translate genetic instructions. They often act as hormones, messengers, or regulators of important processes.
Nonribosomal Peptides
These peptides are created by specialized enzymes rather than ribosomal translation. They are often more complex and may form ring-like structures.
Milk Peptides and Peptones
Milk peptides come from milk proteins and can be released during digestion or fermentation. Peptones are derived from milk or meat and are used in laboratories as nutrient sources.
Peptide Fragments
These are smaller pieces of larger proteins, created naturally in the body or intentionally in the lab. Researchers study peptide fragments to understand protein function and develop targeted research tools.
Important Peptide Terms

Understanding a few key terms makes working with peptides much easier. Here’s a quick guide:

Amino Acids
The building blocks of peptides and proteins. Think of them as the alphabet used to “spell” all peptides.
Cyclic Peptides
Peptides that form a ring-like structure rather than a straight chain, often making them more stable and resistant to breakdown.
Peptide Sequence
The exact order of amino acids in a peptide — like the unique “fingerprint” of that molecule.
Peptide Bond
The strong chemical link that connects two amino acids together, created through a natural reaction where water is released.
Peptide Mapping
A quality-control process used to confirm the exact sequence of a peptide or protein by breaking it down and analyzing the pattern.
Peptide Mimetics
Lab-created molecules that imitate natural peptides, often used in research involving hormones, enzymes, and immune responses.
Peptide Fingerprint
A unique chromatographic pattern produced when a peptide is partially broken down and analyzed, helping researchers verify its identity.
Peptide Library
A large collection of peptides with different amino acid combinations, used for research and drug discovery to identify new therapeutic candidates.

At IonLabPeptides.com, we believe that knowledge is power — especially when it comes to science. Our peptides are offered exclusively for in-vitro research purposes, giving scientists reliable tools to explore breakthroughs in medicine, biology, and biotechnology.

Important Notice: Our peptides are not approved for human or animal use, nor are they intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. They are strictly for laboratory research and educational applications.

Chemical link
A peptide bond connects amino acids together to form a peptide chain.
Condensation reaction
The bond forms when water is released as amino acids connect.
Stable structure
Peptide bonds help create strong, organized chains used in biological systems.
What is a Peptide Bond?

A peptide bond is the special chemical link that connects two amino acids together — essentially the “glue” that forms a peptide chain.

This bond forms when the carboxyl group of one amino acid reacts with the amino group of another, releasing a molecule of water in a process called condensation. The result is a stable CO–NH connection, which is what scientists call a peptide bond.

This bond is what transforms individual amino acids into peptides and, eventually, proteins — the very foundation of life’s biological processes.

Peptide Bond Formation

To form a peptide bond, the two amino acids must be aligned so that the carboxyl group of one can react with the amino group of the other. When they bond, a molecule of water is released — this is called a condensation reaction. This process creates a stable link, forming the smallest possible peptide, known as a dipeptide — just two amino acids connected.

Peptide bond formation occurs when amino acids connect and water is released during condensation.

Once this bond is formed, additional amino acids can join the chain to create longer peptides. In general:

Chains of 50 or fewer amino acids are called peptides.
Chains of 50–100 amino acids are called polypeptides.
Chains of more than 100 amino acids are typically considered proteins.

Peptide bonds can also be broken down through hydrolysis, a chemical reaction with water that releases energy. This is why peptide bonds, though strong, are considered metastable — they can break under certain conditions.

Inside living organisms, enzymes can both form and break peptide bonds. Many hormones, antibiotics, and neurotransmitters in the body are peptides, while larger chains are classified as proteins.

Structure of the Peptide Bond

Scientists have studied peptide bonds in great detail, even using x-ray diffraction to better understand their structure. These studies reveal that peptide bonds are rigid and flat — also called planar — rather than flexible.

Amino acid and peptide bond structure showing the chemical connection that forms peptide chains.

This is because of the resonance effect — the electrons in the nitrogen of the amide group interact with the carbonyl group, which stabilizes the bond and gives it partial double-bond character. As a result:

Shorter N–C bond
The N–C bond in the peptide is shorter than a normal single bond.
Slightly longer C=O bond
The C=O bond is slightly longer than in a typical carbonyl.
Trans configuration
The peptide chain adopts a more stable trans configuration that avoids steric clashes.
This unique structure is what gives peptides their strength and consistency, allowing them to form reliable chains in proteins.
The Polarity of the Peptide Bond

Peptide bonds also have an electrical polarity due to the way electrons are distributed. The carbonyl oxygen carries a slight negative charge, while the amide nitrogen carries a slight positive charge.

This charge separation makes the peptide bond act like a permanent dipole and contributes to its partial double-bond nature. The result is a bond that is rigid and less flexible, preventing free rotation — an important feature for maintaining the overall shape of proteins and peptides.

Important Notice: Our peptides are not approved for human or animal use, nor are they intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. They are strictly for laboratory research and educational applications.

Research-ready output
Multi-step purification supports high purity, consistency, and reliable research use.
Why Peptide Purification Matters

In the modern era, huge leaps forward in the scientific field of peptide synthesis have enabled the production of custom peptides on an immense scale. With the increased production of synthetic peptides for research, the implementation of effective peptide purification methods has only become more critical. For more information on how IonPeptide ensures that every peptide on our website exceeds 99% purity, see our Peptide Purity page. This page details various aspects of peptide purification that take place during peptide synthesis, different purification methods and strategies, and the possible impurities that can be removed through purification.

Peptides are complex molecules, and this complexity can make other common purification methods less effective. During synthesis, special attention must be paid to maximizing both efficiency and yield to provide customers with the purest possible peptide at the lowest possible cost. While crystallization works well for many compounds, peptide purification most often relies on chromatography — particularly high-pressure reversed-phase chromatography — to achieve exceptional purity.

Removing Specific Impurities From Peptides

When it comes to research, purity is everything — even small impurities can throw off results. Different applications require different minimum purity levels, but in general, the higher the purity, the more reliable the results. For example, in vitro studies typically require over 95% purity, whereas less sensitive tests like ELISA titers may allow for lower levels.

During peptide synthesis, several types of impurities can form, such as:

Hydrolysis products from unstable amide bonds.
Deletion sequences from solid-phase synthesis.
Diastereomers and insertion peptides from side reactions.
By-products from protection group removal.
Polymeric or cyclic peptides formed as unwanted byproducts.
Our purification process is designed to detect and remove each of these impurities, leaving behind only the exact peptide sequence you ordered — nothing more, nothing less.
Peptide Purification Strategy

We keep our purification process as efficient and precise as possible. In many cases, two or more purification steps are performed sequentially to achieve ultra-high purity.

STEP 01
Capture step

The process generally starts with a capture step, which removes most impurities produced during synthesis.

STEP 02
Polishing step

This is followed by a polishing step — often using techniques like ion exchange and reversed-phase chromatography — to eliminate even trace contaminants.

This multi-step approach ensures that the final peptide you receive is highly pure, consistent, and research-ready, meeting the most demanding scientific standards.
Peptide Purification Processes

Purifying peptides is a complex, multi-step process that involves several specialized systems — from buffer preparation and solvent delivery to fractionation and advanced data collection. At the heart of it all is the chromatography column, which plays a critical role in determining the final outcome.

Our columns are built with precision using glass or steel and optimized for maximum efficiency, whether using static or dynamic compression modes. Every step is conducted under strict Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) to ensure quality, consistency, and the highest standards of cleanliness and safety.

Affinity Chromatography (AC)

Affinity Chromatography is a powerful method that isolates peptides based on their specific interaction with a ligand attached to a chromatographic matrix. The desired peptide binds to the ligand, while unbound material is washed away.

Because this binding is reversible, we can change conditions — like pH or polarity — to release the purified peptide. This method delivers exceptional resolution and is ideal when high purity and selectivity are required.

Ion Exchange Chromatography (IEX)

Ion Exchange Chromatography separates peptides based on their electrical charge. Peptides are loaded into a column where they bind to a medium with the opposite charge. Then, by gradually altering the salt concentration or pH, each peptide is eluted at its precise point — resulting in a highly purified product.

IEX is known for its high resolution and capacity, making it a go-to method for isolating peptides that need to be free of even trace contaminants.

Hydrophobic Interaction Chromatography (HIC)

Hydrophobic Interaction Chromatography separates peptides based on their affinity for hydrophobic surfaces. Peptides are loaded onto a column where they bind to the hydrophobic medium in a high-salt environment. Then, by gradually lowering the salt concentration, peptides are released and collected in a purified form.

HIC is particularly effective as a second-step purification after another method like ion exchange. It offers good resolution and capacity, making it a powerful option for producing highly pure peptides.

Gel Filtration (GF)

Gel Filtration, also known as size-exclusion chromatography, isolates peptides based on molecular size. Larger molecules flow through the column faster, while smaller ones take longer to pass through. GF is best suited for small-volume samples and provides excellent resolution when precise separation is required.

Reversed Phase Chromatography (RPC)

Reversed Phase Chromatography is known for its exceptional resolution and is one of the most common methods for polishing peptides to very high purity. Peptides bind to a hydrophobic column matrix and are gradually eluted using organic solvents, such as acetonitrile.

Because this method provides such a strong binding interaction, it’s excellent for analytical applications like peptide mapping. However, since organic solvents can sometimes denature peptides, RPC is generally used as a final polishing step rather than when peptide activity or structural recovery is required.

Compliance with GMP

At IonLabPeptides.com, we follow the most stringent Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) to ensure that every peptide we produce is of the highest quality and consistency. GMP compliance means that all chemical and analytical procedures are carefully documented, controlled, and repeatable — so you can trust that your results are reliable.

Because purification is one of the final steps in peptide production, it has a major impact on the overall quality of the final product. That’s why we monitor and control every critical parameter, including:

Column loading and flow rate
Column performance and cleaning procedures
Elution buffer composition
Process timing and storage conditions
Fraction pooling and recovery
Our dedication to these rigorous standards allows us to consistently deliver peptides that exceed 99% purity and meet the requirements of even the most demanding research applications.

At IonLabPeptides.com, we know that purity is the foundation of reliable research. That’s why every peptide we produce exceeds 99% purity — giving scientists confidence that their results are accurate and reproducible.

HPLC and Mass Spectrometry

High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) is one of the most trusted scientific methods for separating, identifying, and precisely measuring the components of a mixture. This advanced technique ensures that every peptide we produce meets the highest purity standards.

Mass Spectrometry (MS) takes verification a step further by confirming the exact molecular weight and identity of each peptide. It works by ionizing the sample, sorting the ions based on their mass-to-charge ratio, and generating a unique “fingerprint” that proves the peptide’s authenticity.

At IonLabPeptides.com, we don’t just test once — we test at every stage of the production process. This rigorous, step-by-step approach guarantees that every peptide is exactly what you ordered, with the purity and accuracy required for reliable research results.

Choosing the right solvent depends on the peptide’s amino acid composition and charge.
Small test first
Solubility should be tested with a small amount before dissolving the full sample.
Stability matters
Careful dissolving, aliquoting, and storage help protect peptide stability and activity.
What Factors Determine Peptide Solubility?

Choosing the right solvent can sometimes be one of the trickiest parts of working with synthetic peptides. Many peptides dissolve easily in sterile water, but others — especially those with long chains of hydrophobic, water-repelling amino acids — can be harder to work with.

A peptide’s solubility depends on the physical properties of its amino acids, which can be grouped into four categories: basic, acidic, polar uncharged, and non-polar.

Non-Polar / Hydrophobic Amino Acids
These do not dissolve well in water. Peptides containing many of them generally dissolve better in organic solvents like DMSO, propanol, isopropanol, methanol, or DMF.
Acidic Amino Acids
These peptides are best dissolved in basic solutions, such as ammonium hydroxide, though this should not be used for peptides containing cysteine.
Basic Amino Acids
These are usually dissolved in acidic solvents, such as acetic acid solution.
Short Peptides
Peptides with fewer than 5 residues usually dissolve easily in water, so always try water first before moving to other solvents.
Understanding your peptide’s amino acid composition can save time, minimize trial-and-error, and help you achieve the correct solution quickly.
Peptide Solubility Guidelines

When working with synthetic peptides, it is always best to test solubility with a small amount first. This helps avoid wasting material if the peptide does not dissolve as expected.

Here are a few best practices:

Bring to Room Temperature
Allow peptides to reach room temperature before attempting to dissolve them.
Start with Sterile Water
Always try dissolving in sterile water first.
Try Removable Solvents
If water does not work, try solvents that can later be removed through lyophilization or freeze-drying.
Restart if Needed
If the first attempt fails, lyophilization allows you to restart without losing or damaging the peptide.
Assist Dissolution Carefully
Use mild warming below 40°C / 104°F or sonication to help dissolve stubborn peptides. These methods will not change inherent solubility but can speed up the process.
Following these steps helps ensure your peptide dissolves effectively without compromising its integrity.
Predicting Peptide Solubility Characteristics

You can often predict whether a peptide will be acidic, basic, or neutral — and therefore which solvent is best — by looking at its amino acid composition. Here is a simple way to estimate:

Assign −1 to Acidic Amino Acids: These include Asp (D), Glu (E), and C-terminal COOH.
Assign +1 to Basic Amino Acids: These include Lys (K), Arg (R), and N-terminal NH₂.
Add +1 for Each Histidine (H): Count only those that would be charged at pH 6.
Calculate the Net Charge: Add all the values to find the peptide’s overall net charge.
Knowing the net charge helps predict which type of solvent — acidic, basic, or neutral — will most likely dissolve the peptide successfully.
Dissolving the Peptide in Solution

Once you have calculated the peptide’s net charge, you can move on to dissolving it. Always start by trying sterile water first. If the peptide does not dissolve, follow these guidelines:

Positively Charged Peptides
Use acetic acid solution, usually 10–30%. If still unsuccessful, try trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) at a very small amount.
Negatively Charged Peptides
Use ammonium hydroxide. If the peptide contains cysteine, avoid ammonium hydroxide and instead add a small amount of DMF.
Neutral Peptides
Use organic solvents such as acetonitrile, methanol, or isopropanol. For highly hydrophobic peptides, try dissolving in a small amount of DMSO.
Note: Peptides with cysteine, methionine, or tryptophan are prone to oxidation in DMSO. If peptides form gels, add 6M guanidine-HCl or 8M urea to help them dissolve.

After the peptide is dissolved:

Dilute Carefully: Slowly add the solution to a buffered solution with gentle mixing to avoid localized concentration spikes.
Prepare Higher-Concentration Stocks: Make stock solutions stronger than the working concentration, then dilute further for assays.
Aliquot & Store Properly: Divide into smaller portions and store at −20°C (−4°F). For peptides containing cysteine, methionine, or tryptophan, store in an oxygen-free environment to prevent oxidation.
For best results, follow these steps to ensure your peptide is fully dissolved without compromising its stability or activity.

Cold & dry storage

Freeze-thaw control

Lyophilized stability

Best Practices For Storing Peptides

Proper storage is essential for keeping peptides stable, potent, and ready for reliable research use. By following best practices, you can extend peptide shelf life, prevent degradation, and protect the integrity of your experiments.

General storage guidelines:

Keep Cold and Protected from Light
Once received, peptides should be stored in a cool, dark environment.
Short-Term Storage — Days to Weeks
Refrigerate peptides at 4°C / 39°F. Lyophilized peptides are typically stable at room temperature for 30–60 days, but refrigerating them ensures maximum stability.
Long-Term Storage — Months to Years
Freeze peptides at −80°C / −112°F whenever possible to maintain stability for years.
Avoid Freeze-Thaw Cycles
Repeated freezing and thawing can degrade peptides. Instead, aliquot solutions into small portions before freezing.
Avoid Frost-Free Freezers
Frost-free freezers fluctuate in temperature during defrost cycles, which can harm peptide stability.
Lyophilized peptides are generally best for longer storage, while reconstituted peptides require more careful short-term handling.
Preventing Oxidation and Moisture Contamination

Peptides are highly sensitive to air and moisture, which can cause them to degrade or lose potency. To protect your peptides:

Avoid Moisture
Always let peptides warm to room temperature before opening after freezer storage. This prevents condensation from forming on the container or peptide.
Limit Air Exposure
Open containers only as long as needed, then reseal them tightly. For maximum protection, store under a dry, inert gas such as nitrogen or argon to reduce oxidation risk.
Watch Sensitive Sequences
Peptides containing cysteine (C), methionine (M), or tryptophan (W) are especially prone to oxidation and need extra care.
Aliquot for Convenience
Divide peptides into smaller vials before storage so you only open what you need — reducing repeated air exposure and freeze-thaw cycles.
These steps can significantly extend your peptide’s stability and preserve its activity for long-term use.
Storing Peptides In Solution

Peptides are most stable when lyophilized, or freeze-dried. Once dissolved, their shelf life is shorter and they are more vulnerable to bacterial contamination — especially peptides containing Cys, Met, Trp, Asp, Gln, and N-terminal Glu.

If you must store peptides in solution:

Use Sterile Buffers at pH 5–8
A properly buffered sterile solution can help protect the peptide during short-term storage.
Aliquot to Avoid Repeated Cycles
Divide the solution into smaller portions to prevent repeated freeze-thaw cycles.
Short-Term Refrigeration
Store refrigerated at 4°C / 39°F for short-term use, generally up to 30 days.
Keep Unstable Peptides Frozen
Keep unstable peptides frozen when not in use to maintain integrity.
For longer storage, lyophilized peptide is the preferred format whenever possible.
Peptide Storage Containers

Storage containers should be clean, clear, structurally sound, and chemically resistant. Both glass and plastic vials can be used, but container choice matters for long-term stability.

Polystyrene Vials
Polystyrene vials are clear but not highly resistant to solvents.
Polypropylene Vials
Polypropylene vials are more chemically resistant and translucent.
Glass Vials
Glass vials are ideal for long-term storage but may need protective sleeves to avoid breakage.
Transfer When Needed
If peptides are initially shipped in plastic vials, you can transfer them to glass containers for optimal long-term stability.
Peptide Storage Guidelines: General Tips

When storing peptides, keep these best practices in mind:

Store Cold and Dry
Keep peptides in a cool, dark place away from moisture.
Minimize Freeze-Thaw Cycles
Aliquot into smaller portions to avoid repeatedly thawing and refreezing.
Limit Air Exposure
Open containers only when necessary and reseal quickly.
Protect from Light
Light can degrade peptides over time, so keep them shielded.
Avoid Long-Term Storage in Solution
Whenever possible, store peptides lyophilized and freeze-dried.
Aliquot by Experimental Needs
Divide into amounts you’ll use per experiment for convenience and stability.
Following these simple steps helps maintain peptide integrity and ensures reliable, reproducible results in your research.

Peptide Synthesis
BY PEPTIDE INFORMATION

At IonLabPeptides.com, we believe that knowledge is power — especially when it comes to science. Our peptides are offered exclusively for in-vitro research purposes, giving scientists reliable tools to explore breakthroughs in medicine, biology, and biotechnology.

Important Notice: Our peptides are not approved for human or animal use, nor are they intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. They are strictly for laboratory research and educational applications.

Amino acid linking
Peptide synthesis builds peptides by connecting amino acids through peptide bonds.
Controlled chemistry
Protecting groups help prevent unwanted side reactions and reduced purity.
Research precision
Modern synthesis supports custom peptide design for research and biotechnology.
What is Peptide Synthesis?

Peptide synthesis is the process of building peptides by linking amino acids together through peptide bonds. Thanks to advancements in chemistry and technology, this process has become far more efficient than when it was first developed — allowing researchers to create highly precise, custom peptides for a wide range of applications.

Today, synthetic peptides play an essential role in scientific research, drug discovery, and medical innovation. As the field of peptide science continues to grow, peptide synthesis remains at the heart of groundbreaking discoveries that drive progress in health and biotechnology.

Solid-phase peptide synthesis uses controlled chemistry to build peptide chains step by step.
How Peptides are Synthesized?

Peptides are created by linking amino acids together — usually by attaching the carboxyl group, or C-terminus, of one amino acid to the amino group, or N-terminus, of another. Unlike how peptides are built naturally in living organisms, synthetic peptide synthesis follows a controlled C-to-N direction, allowing scientists to build custom peptides with precision.

Because there are 20 naturally occurring amino acids — and many more that can be synthesized — the possibilities for new peptide designs are nearly endless. However, peptide synthesis is a delicate process. Amino acids have reactive groups that, if left uncontrolled, can lead to unwanted byproducts, truncated chains, or reduced purity.

To prevent these issues, chemists use protecting groups — temporary chemical shields that keep certain parts of the amino acid from reacting until the right moment:

N-terminal protecting groups
Shield the N-terminus so the peptide can be built step by step. Common examples include Boc and Fmoc.
C-terminal protecting groups
Used in some synthesis methods, such as liquid-phase synthesis, to control reactivity at the carboxyl end.
Side chain protecting groups
Safeguard reactive side chains to prevent unwanted side reactions. These are removed at the end of synthesis.
Thanks to these controlled methods, researchers can create highly accurate and reproducible peptides for research, drug development, and beyond.
Peptide Synthesis Processes

Peptides can be made using different methods, but today’s gold standard is Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis (SPPS). While older solution-phase synthesis is still occasionally used for large-scale production, SPPS is preferred because it offers higher yield, better purity, and faster turnaround times.

SPPS follows a simple, step-by-step cycle:

Step 01
Attach the first amino acid to a solid polymer resin.
Step 02
Protect reactive groups to prevent unwanted side reactions.
Step 03
Couple the next amino acid to the growing chain.
Step 04
Deprotect to expose the next reaction site.
Step 05
Release the finished peptide from the resin.
Final Quality Step
Purify and verify the peptide to confirm identity, quality, and purity.

This process is repeated until the peptide is complete. For longer peptides, microwave-assisted SPPS can speed up reactions and improve yields, though it is often more expensive.

Even with the precision of SPPS, small impurities can still occur, especially in longer peptides. That’s why every batch undergoes advanced purification, most commonly using Reverse-Phase Chromatography (RPC) and High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), to separate and remove unwanted byproducts — ensuring you receive peptides of the highest quality and purity.

The Value of Synthetic Peptides

Synthetic peptides are at the heart of modern biomedical research. Their ability to mimic natural biological processes makes them invaluable tools for understanding disease, developing new treatments, and driving pharmaceutical innovation.

Pharmaceutical companies have already developed several FDA-approved drugs derived from peptides, proving their effectiveness and safety. Thanks to their specificity, low toxicity, and versatility, peptides continue to play a key role in everything from basic research to clinical applications.

As science advances, synthetic peptides will remain a cornerstone of discovery — helping researchers and companies alike develop better therapies, diagnostics, and breakthroughs that improve health worldwide.

Specificity
Peptides can be designed to interact with targeted biological pathways.
Versatility
They support research across biotechnology, drug discovery, and molecular biology.
Innovation
Synthetic peptides continue to support new discoveries and future therapeutic research.

Peptides vs Proteins
BY PEPTIDE INFORMATION

At IonLabPeptides.com, we believe that knowledge is power — especially when it comes to science. Our peptides are offered exclusively for in-vitro research purposes, giving scientists reliable tools to explore breakthroughs in medicine, biology, and biotechnology.

Important Notice: Our peptides are not approved for human or animal use, nor are they intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. They are strictly for laboratory research and educational applications.

Size difference
Peptides are usually shorter amino acid chains, while proteins are larger and more complex.
Structure difference
Proteins often fold into stable 3D shapes, while shorter peptides may remain simpler or less structured.
Function difference
Peptides often act as signals or regulators, while proteins commonly perform specialized functions.
What are the Differences?

Peptides and proteins are closely related, but they’re not the same. While both are made of amino acids — the building blocks of life — they differ in size, structure, and biological function.

The term “peptide” is sometimes used interchangeably with “protein,” but peptides are typically shorter chains of amino acids, whereas proteins are much larger and more complex molecules that often fold into specific 3D shapes to carry out specialized tasks in the body.

Understanding the relationship between amino acids, peptides, and proteins is key to appreciating how they work together in biological systems — and why peptides are so important for research, diagnostics, and therapeutic development.

Amino acids form peptides, and longer or folded chains can become proteins.
Amino acid
The smallest building block in this relationship, containing an amino group, carboxyl group, and side chain.
Peptide
A shorter chain of amino acids connected by peptide bonds.
Protein
A larger, more complex molecule that often folds into a stable structure with a specialized function.
Amino Acids

Amino acids are small but incredibly important molecules that make up peptides and proteins. Each amino acid contains an amino group (NH₂), a carboxyl group (COOH), and a unique side chain that gives it distinct chemical properties.

When amino acids link together through amide (peptide) bonds, they form peptides. The smallest peptide, made of two amino acids, is called a dipeptide. Three form a tripeptide, and so on. These simple connections create the foundation for everything from short peptides to large, complex proteins.

Amino group
One of the key chemical groups found in amino acids.
Carboxyl group
The group that can react with another amino acid during peptide bond formation.
Side chain
The unique part of each amino acid that gives it distinct chemical behavior.
Peptide bond
The connection that joins amino acids together to create peptide chains.
Peptides

Peptides are short chains of amino acids connected by peptide bonds. They can range from just two amino acids to several dozen.

Oligopeptides: Typically fewer than 10 amino acids.
Polypeptides: More than 10 amino acids, forming longer chains that may fold into more complex shapes.

Peptides play a crucial role in biological processes, acting as messengers, regulators, and building blocks for larger proteins.

In simple terms, peptides sit between individual amino acids and larger protein structures.
Polypeptides and Proteins

Polypeptides are simply longer peptide chains, generally 40–50 amino acids or more. Once a polypeptide reaches a certain length and folds into a stable 3D structure, it becomes a protein.

Proteins: Usually perform a specific function, such as hemoglobin transporting oxygen in the blood.
Shorter Polypeptides: Often remain unstructured and do not form a stable shape.

Understanding this distinction is essential, as it explains why proteins are functionally more specialized while peptides often serve as regulators or signals.

Polypeptide
A longer peptide chain that may or may not fold into a stable structure.
Protein
A longer, structurally defined molecule that usually performs a specialized biological function.
Peptide Vs. Protein: Which Term to Use?

Technically, all proteins are made from polypeptide chains — but not all polypeptides are proteins. In research and product descriptions, the term “peptide” usually refers to shorter amino acid chains, fewer than about 50 amino acids, while “protein” refers to longer, structurally defined molecules.

This distinction helps researchers and clinicians communicate clearly about the molecules they are studying or using in experiments.

Use “peptide” when
The molecule is a shorter amino acid chain, often fewer than about 50 amino acids.
Use “protein” when
The molecule is longer, folded, structurally defined, and usually function-specific.
The easiest way to explain the difference: all proteins are built from amino acid chains, but not every amino acid chain is a protein.

At IonLabPeptides.com, we believe that knowledge is power — especially when it comes to science. Our peptides are offered exclusively for in-vitro research purposes, giving scientists reliable tools to explore breakthroughs in medicine, biology, and biotechnology.

Important Notice: Our peptides are not approved for human or animal use, nor are they intended to diagnose, treat, or cure any disease. They are strictly for laboratory research and educational applications.

Scientific study
Research peptides are peptides used in controlled scientific and laboratory research.
In-vitro use
They are not medicines and are intended for laboratory research use only.
Discovery support
They help researchers study biological functions, molecular pathways, and future compounds.
What are Research Peptides?
Research peptides are used in controlled scientific study and laboratory research settings.

Research peptides are simply peptides used in scientific study.

Over the past few years, they have become increasingly important thanks to their high selectivity, effectiveness, and safety.

Because of their ability to interact with biological systems in precise ways, research peptides are now at the center of pharmaceutical innovation — helping scientists explore new treatments, improve patient outcomes, and discover next-generation therapeutics. The growing interest in peptides has led to a surge in demand, fueling rapid progress across medical and biochemical research.

Research peptides are valuable because they allow scientists to study highly specific biological interactions in controlled laboratory environments.
Research Peptides vs Medicines?

It’s important to understand that research peptides are not medicines — they are intended strictly for in-vitro research use, meaning studies performed outside the body.

Scientists use research peptides to:

Explore New Therapeutics
Discover potential peptide-based drugs.
Test Biological Functions
Study cell signaling, enzyme reactions, and molecular pathways.
Develop Future Medicines
Create and refine compounds that may one day move into clinical trials.

While many peptide-based medicines have already been approved by the FDA — such as Lupron™ for prostate cancer and Victoza™ for type 2 diabetes — these are not research peptides. Approved drugs have undergone extensive testing, clinical trials, and FDA review to ensure they are safe and effective for patients.

Research peptides, on the other hand, are strictly for controlled lab use and are not approved to diagnose, treat, or cure any medical condition. Their purpose is to generate data that could lead to tomorrow’s breakthroughs.

The simple distinction: approved medicines are for patient use; research peptides are for controlled laboratory research only.
Research Peptides as Future Therapeutics

More than 7,000 naturally occurring peptides have already been discovered, and their potential in human health is enormous. Acting as hormones, growth factors, neurotransmitters, ion channel ligands, and anti-infectives, peptides serve as highly selective signaling molecules with precise biological effects.

In clinical studies, peptides have demonstrated remarkable safety, tolerability, and potency — while also offering predictable metabolism and high selectivity. This makes them one of the most promising frontiers for therapeutic development.

Selective signaling
Peptides can interact with biological pathways in highly specific ways.
Research foundation
Today’s laboratory peptide research may support tomorrow’s scientific breakthroughs.
Key Areas of Research and Application

Research peptides are being studied across multiple fields where precision, selectivity, and controlled biological interaction are important.

Metabolic Diseases
Peptides are being studied for type 2 diabetes and related metabolic disorders, particularly as obesity and diabetes rates continue to rise globally.
Oncology
Research is exploring peptide-based therapies as alternatives or additions to traditional chemotherapy, driven by the need for more targeted, less toxic treatments.
Infectious and Rare Diseases
Peptides show promise in fighting infections, inflammation, and rare conditions where conventional drugs may fall short.
Diagnostics & Vaccines
Beyond treatment, peptides are also being investigated for advanced diagnostics and next-generation vaccines.

Ultimately, the development of tomorrow’s peptide-based medicines depends on today’s research peptides. These molecules form the foundation for experimentation, innovation, and therapeutic discovery in the lab.

Research peptides should always be framed clearly as laboratory-use materials, not products for human or animal use.

Privacy Policy

IonLabPeptides.com is committed to protecting your privacy and maintaining transparency about how we collect, use, and safeguard your personal information when you use our website, products, or services.

Read Policy
Privacy Request
Policy Snapshot

This policy explains the data Ion Peptide may collect, how that data is used, when it may be shared with service providers, and how customers may exercise privacy-related rights.

EFFECTIVE DATE
January 1, 2025
LAST UPDATED
October 01, 2025
CONTACT
support@ionlabpeptides.com
DATA
Information Collected

Personal, technical, marketing, cart, and session data may be collected.

USE
How Data Is Used

Data supports orders, shipping, service, communications, fraud prevention, and compliance.

SMS
Consent & Marketing

Email and SMS communications require consent, with clear opt-out options.

RIGHT
Your Rights

Users may request access, correction, deletion, portability, or processing restrictions.

HOW WE HANDLE DATA
Clear, secure, and consent-aware

This privacy page should feel calm and trustworthy. The goal is to clearly explain what information is collected, why it is used, how it is protected, and how customers can contact Ion Peptide about privacy-related requests.

Order-focused data use

Customer information is used to process and fulfill orders, provide support, send shipping updates, and support transactional communications.

Security-minded handling

Ion Peptide uses SSL encryption, PCI-compliant payment processing, and restricted internal access to help protect customer data.

Privacy rights access

Depending on jurisdiction, users may request access, correction, deletion, a copy of data, or restriction of certain processing activities.

01
Information We Collect

We may collect the following categories of information:

Personal Information
Name, email address, and phone number
Billing and shipping addresses
Payment information, processed securely via third-party providers
Technical & Usage Data
IP address, browser type, device type, and operating system
Website behavior, clicks, page visits, referring URLs, and time spent on pages
Marketing & Communication Preferences
Opt-in status for promotional emails or SMS
Responses to marketing campaigns
Cart and Session Data
Items added to your shopping cart
Session behavior used to trigger reminder messages for abandoned carts
02
How We Use Your Information

We use collected data to:

Process and fulfill orders, including shipping and delivery
Provide and improve customer service
Send order confirmations, shipping updates, and transactional notifications
Deliver marketing communications with your explicit consent
Detect fraud and comply with applicable legal obligations
03
Marketing Communications: Email & SMS
Consent

By providing your email or phone number, you consent to receive:

Promotional offers via email and/or SMS
Order-related updates such as confirmation and tracking messages
SMS Data Use & Consent

Phone numbers provided may be used for:

Order confirmations, shipping updates, and cart reminder messages
Communication via our SMS service provider for delivery
Opt-Out Options
Click the unsubscribe link in any promotional email
Reply “STOP” to any SMS to opt out of further marketing messages
Note: Opting out of marketing messages does not prevent essential order-related or legal communications.
04
Data Protection & Security

We employ industry-standard security measures, including:

SSL encryption for secure data transmission
PCI-compliant payment processing
Restricted internal access to customer data

While we make every effort to secure your information, no online system is completely secure. By using our services, you accept the inherent risks of internet-based transactions.

05
Sharing Your Information

We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal data. We only share information when necessary for:

Payment processing
Shipping and logistics
Email and SMS communication platforms
Third-party disclosure exceptions
Sharing may occur when required by law or to protect our legal rights
SMS opt-in consent data is never shared with third parties
06
Cookies & Tracking Technologies

We use cookies and similar technologies to:

Enhance website functionality and usability
Personalize browsing experiences
Track site performance and analytics
Monitor shopping cart activity, including abandoned carts, to trigger reminders

You may manage or disable cookies in your browser settings. Continued use of our website constitutes consent to our use of cookies.

07
Your Rights

Depending on your jurisdiction, you may have the right to:

Access personal data we hold about you
Correct or update inaccurate data
Request deletion of personal data, subject to legal retention requirements
Receive a copy of your data in a portable format
Object to or restrict certain processing activities
To exercise your rights, please contact us using the information below. Verified requests are typically addressed within 30 days.
08
Data Retention

We retain personal data only as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes described in this policy, including:

Legal, accounting, or tax obligations
Afterward, data is securely deleted or anonymized
09
Third-Party Websites

Our site may include links to third-party websites. We are not responsible for their content, privacy practices, or security measures. Review their policies before sharing personal information.

10
Children’s Privacy

We do not knowingly collect information from individuals under 18. If we discover such data has been submitted, it will be promptly deleted.

11
Changes to This Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy at any time. Changes will be posted with a revised “Last Updated” date. Continued use of our services constitutes acceptance of the updated policy.

12
Governing Law and Jurisdiction

This Privacy Policy is governed by the laws of the State of New Mexico and the United States. By using our website, you agree to submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of courts located in New Mexico for any disputes.

13
Contact Information

For privacy-related inquiries or requests, please contact:

Email: support@ionlabpeptides.com

Items must be unopened, unused, and in original condition.

If you receive a damaged, defective, or incorrect product:

Email us within 48 hours of delivery with clear photographs of the item(s).
We will promptly review the claim and, if approved, ship a replacement at no cost.

Claims submitted after the 48-hour review window may be limited or denied depending on the circumstances.

Final Notes

Refuse returns that do not meet eligibility criteria.
Deny returns suspected of policy abuse or fraudulent activity.

SHIPPING FLOW
How your shipment moves

This page is designed to help customers understand when orders ship, how tracking works, and where carrier limitations may affect delivery.

01
Order Placed

Your order is submitted through checkout with your selected shipping method.

02
Cutoff Review

Orders placed before 5:00 PM EST on business days are typically handled the same day.

03
Carrier Handoff

The order is prepared and handed to the selected or applicable shipping carrier.

Delivery

Delivery timing depends on the selected service, destination, carrier, and external conditions.

01
Complimentary Shipping

We offer free 2 Day FedEx / UPS on all domestic U.S. orders over $250+.

Note: Complimentary shipping applies to qualifying domestic U.S. orders and may depend on order value, available carrier service, and checkout conditions.
02
Same-Day Shipping Cutoff

Orders placed before 5:00 PM EST on business days are typically shipped the same day. Orders received after 5:00 PM EST are shipped on the next business day.

We strive to process and fulfill orders as quickly as possible, but same-day shipping is not guaranteed during high-volume periods, holidays, or due to unforeseen logistics issues.

Important: Same-day shipping depends on order timing, business-day processing, carrier availability, and operational volume.
03
Expedited Shipping Options

For faster delivery, customers may select upgraded shipping methods at checkout:

UPS / FedEx Express 2 Day
UPS / FedEx Next Day Delivery

Shipping speed is determined by your chosen service and destination. All delivery timelines are estimates provided by the carrier.

04
Carrier Selection & PO Boxes

We ship using UPS, FedEx, and United States Postal Service (USPS).

Important:

UPS cannot deliver to PO Box addresses.
FedEx cannot deliver to PO Box addresses.
Please use a physical delivery address when selecting UPS or FedEx to avoid delays, returned shipments, or carrier delivery issues.
05
Tracking & Delivery Confirmation

Once your order is shipped, you will receive a tracking number via email. This number can be used to monitor your shipment’s progress directly through the carrier’s website.

If tracking shows a package as delivered but you did not receive it, please contact the carrier directly before reaching out to our support team.

06
Shipping Liability Disclaimer

Ion Peptide is not responsible for:

Carrier delays, errors, or lost/stolen packages
Delivery to incorrect addresses due to customer error
Weather-related delays or force majeure events
Customs delays or international transit issues, if applicable

While we will always assist in tracking or escalating issues with carriers, we cannot offer refunds for shipping problems beyond our control.

Important: Carrier timelines, delivery scans, weather delays, and delivery exceptions may fall outside Ion Peptide’s direct control.
07
Address Accuracy & Order Review

Please ensure that all shipping information is accurate at checkout. Incorrect addresses may lead to delivery issues, return-to-sender fees, or restocking delays.

If you realize there is an error, contact us immediately after placing your order.

08
Questions?

For questions related to your shipment, expedited services, carrier limitations, delivery status, or tracking issues, please contact Ion Peptide support.

For the fastest support, include your order number, tracking number if available, shipping address, and a short description of the issue.
